- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤ 0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 3–7% to account for mean reversion or short-term rebound.
- If model shows a sharp spike followed by a steep drop (e.g., 10+ point overshoot), reduce forecast by 10–15% in the following 3–5 periods to avoid overcorrection.
- Model consistently underestimates in the first 5–7 days of a new 30-day horizon; add 1–3% to forecast for early period bias.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., 0.67 → 0.33 → 0.67), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with sentiment shift 1–2 periods ahead.
- When sentiment is consistently low (e.g., 0.33 or below for 3+ days), model underperforms; apply a 5–10% upward bias to avoid prolonged underestimation.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overestimates the first 10 days; cap forecast at 10% above historical mean for first 5 days to avoid horizon bias.
